text:
maggie: heads up, I'm landing TF change to give secretstore-sa KMS decrypt/generate permissions for the new object-store service. quick sanity check?
ram: can you paste the policy snippet? want to make sure the Condition matches IRSA principal.
maggie: sure — current plan (simplified):
```hcl
resource "aws_kms_key" "objstore" {
  description = "objstore key"
}
resource "aws_kms_grant" "objstore_irsa" {
  key_id = aws_kms_key.objstore.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.irsa_objstore.arn
  operations = ["Encrypt", "Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
}
resource "aws_iam_role" "irsa_objstore" {
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa.json
}
```
ram: two things: 1) you should be using a condition on the grant or key policy to assert aws:SourceAccount or aws:PrincipalArn? grants don't support Condition the same way — better to adjust the key policy.
olivia: also watch for ordering in TF — the SA annotation -> IRSA role can exist before grant applies, and k8s pods may start and fail for a few minutes. add explicit depends_on from k8s service account shim?
maggie: good points. here's the key_policy snippet I'm planning to add:
```json
{
  "Sid": "AllowIRSAObjstore",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {
    "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedwoodIRSA-objstore"
  },
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt", "kms:Encrypt", "kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*",
  "Condition": {
    "StringLike": {
      "aws:PrincipalArn": "arn:aws:iam::*:role/RedwoodIRSA-*"
    }
  }
}
```
zach: hmm, using StringLike on aws:PrincipalArn is common but IRSA roles are assumed by OIDC; the session principal looks like `arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/RedwoodIRSA-objstore/subject` — Condition should use `sts:arn` pattern or `aws:principalarn` with `assumed-role/*/system:serviceaccount*` depending on what you expect.
ram: yes — try `StringLike: {"aws:PrincipalArn": "arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/RedwoodIRSA-objstore/*"}` or instead scope via `StringEquals: {"kms:EncryptionContext:aws:eks:cluster-name": "redwood-prod"}` if you can set encryption context.
maggie: we don't set encryption context from the service yet. is that recommended?
olivia: encryption context solves a lot for cross-account/role ambiguity, but you need the app to supply it when calling KMS. if that's hard, tighten principal pattern.
terraform-bot: deploy plan check: resource aws_kms_grant.objstore_irsa will be created after aws_iam_role.irsa_objstore, but grants may fail until role propagation finishes — add `lifecycle { create_before_destroy = true }`?
maggie: (typo) meant to say i'll add depends_on = [aws_iam_role.irsa_objstore] on the grant — and include the sts assumed-role ARN pattern in the key policy.
ram: also verify `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn` vs `eks.amazonaws.com/service-account-arn` in your SA annotation. we should be using `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: ${aws_iam_role.irsa_objstore.arn}` on the k8s manifest.
maggie: copied — k8s snippet:
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: secretstore
  namespace: objstore
  annotations:
    eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/RedwoodIRSA-objstore
```
zach: LGTM. after you apply, check pod logs for `AccessDenied` and look for the exact principal shown in the error — that'll tell you if the pattern is wrong.
maggie: will do. I'll push a small follow-up with the exact key policy changes and mark the PR with `infra/irsa-kms` tag. thanks all :thumbsup:
olivia: FYI add a note in the PR about eventual consistency / propagation for reviewers — we've hit false negatives in the past.
terraform-bot: reminder: run `terraform state show aws_kms_key.objstore` to confirm key is the one referenced.
ram: also, if you end up using aws:kms:ViaService conditions for S3 or other services, double-check service principal format (`s3.amazonaws.com`).
maggie: noted. i'll ping if anything flakes during rollout.
